content:
Apple has applied to the court for a preliminary injunction in its ongoing trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI. Apple stated that without a preliminary injunction, the theft of its trade secrets would cause "irreparable harm" to the company.

In the application documents, Apple pointed out that after filing the first lawsuit last month, it had sent a letter to OpenAI, expressing its intention to "seek preliminary injunction relief." However, Apple stated that if OpenAI agrees to the following five requirements, the relevant proceedings can be avoided:

  • Stop accessing or using Apple's confidential information
  • Stop any ongoing use or disclosure activities
  • Preserve all evidence
  • Allow forensic inspection of devices, cloud storage, email, Slack, Teams, and other repositories
  • Search OpenAI's systems for any of Apple's confidential information

According to Apple, OpenAI agreed to the first three requirements, but the two parties failed to reach an agreement on the last two.

Therefore, Apple requests the court to issue a preliminary injunction, asking the judge to immediately prohibit OpenAI from using or obtaining any Apple trade secrets, preserve all evidence, allow Apple to conduct forensic inspections of OpenAI's devices and accounts, and retrieve any Apple confidential information still held by OpenAI.

Apple stated:

Apple also separately filed a motion requesting the court to expedite the discovery process, including advancing the deadline for OpenAI to submit documents, and conducting out-of-court depositions of key OpenAI employees and management.

Along with submitting the above documents, OpenAI also issued its most detailed public response to date regarding Apple's lawsuit. In a blog post released late at night, OpenAI stated that this "frivolous, aggressive, and unusually personally attacking lawsuit" is inconsistent with Apple's reputation as "one of the greatest companies in history."

The injunction hearing is scheduled for October 1, 2026. You can view the complete application documents below.
